projectSummary: The only retrieved record in which a pectoralis major rupture is attributed to a fly-family exercise. One case, so it establishes that the event can occur on a fly machine and nothing about how often. The translation was machine-assisted and not independently checked, so under the frozen U5/EU4 decision this cannot support a decision-critical prose claim on its own.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: n = 1, German language, read through machine-assisted translation with no second independent translation and no fluent-reader check.
The eccentric-phase and steroid statements are the authors' framing of prior literature, not observations from this case.

study.population: A 33-year-old patient of normal habitus sustained a humeral rupture of the pectoralis major during recreational sport. He reported sudden onset of left pectoral pain during training on the chest fly machine, together with a whip-like popping sound, followed by immediate painful restriction of movement in the left arm. There was no history of excessive weight training or anabolic steroid use.

title: [Rupture of the pectoralis major muscle in amateur athletes: a rare injury or often overlooked?].
